angle: Shen He of Half Acre Books explains how an independent bookstore keeps people coming back every month with an annual pass and a Thursday book club instead of discounts, so small-shop owners can work out their own reason for customers to return.

facts.claim: Half Acre Books opened in Hangzhou in 2019: 120 square meters, about 8,000 titles on the shelves.
Since 2021, an annual pass at 399 yuan a year: 10% off books all year, one coffee a month, the book club free.
620 members at the end of 2025, 71% renewal.
facts.source: The shop's membership system export, 2025-12-31 (from Shen He, unaudited)

facts.claim: In 2025 membership fees were 12% of revenue; books 50%, coffee 30%, events 8%.
A book club every Thursday night with 20 seats, free for members, 39 yuan with a drink for everyone else.
A store-wide 50%-off clearance day in 2020 drew people who bought only discounted books and rarely came back.
